page_objective: Define the multilingual behavior, RTL adaptation rules, layout mirroring principles, typography behavior, and localization standards for SIPANEL digital experiences.

multilingual_philosophy.statement: SIPANEL multilingual experiences must preserve engineering clarity, visual consistency, and technical professionalism across all supported languages.

ltr_behavior: Icons and directional indicators follow LTR logic.
rules: Use logical CSS properties instead of hardcoded left/right values.
All layouts must support dynamic direction switching.
Increase line-height slightly for Persian readability.

rtl_navigation: Drawer menus open from opposite side.
language_switcher_rules: Language switcher must remain globally accessible.
Use native language names when possible.

rules: Use logical padding and margin properties.
Preserve equal visual rhythm across languages.

alignment_behavior.technical_labels: May remain LTR when using engineering standards

buttons: Icon direction flips in RTL when directional.
forms: Validation messages align to reading direction.
Phone and email inputs may remain LTR.
tables: Technical data may remain LTR if industry-standard.
General content tables should support RTL alignment.

mixed_language_behavior: English technical abbreviations may remain LTR.
BOM, CAD, RFQ, MTO and similar terms remain untranslated where appropriate.
diagram_rules: Annotations should adapt to reading direction.
Technical arrows flip only when directional meaning changes.

mobile_rules: Allow additional space for translated text expansion.
tablet_and_desktop_rules: Preserve balanced layouts despite language length differences.

requirements: Ensure screen readers recognize language correctly.
Preserve keyboard navigation order in RTL.
Maintain WCAG AA contrast across all languages.

rules: Do not directly machine-translate engineering content without review.
Preserve brand voice across all languages.
Adapt messaging naturally to business culture.
Avoid culturally inappropriate imagery or wording.

forbidden_patterns: Literal translation of engineering terminology without validation
implementation_notes: RTL support must be built into the system architecture from the beginning.
All layouts, components, and interactions must support dynamic direction switching.
Localization quality is critical for technical trust and engineering credibility.
Multilingual consistency must be preserved across website, documentation, forms, and technical diagrams.
